asserts: FTS5 allows efficient searching of a large collection of documents for the subset that contain one or more instances of a search term.
scope: large collections of documents in database applications
not: is not limited to text databases specifically
evidence_excerpt: In their most elementary form, full-text search engines allow the user to efficiently search a large collection of documents for the subset that contain one or more instances of a search term.

asserts: Since version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21), SQLite offers an alternative method for implementing atomic commit and rollback called Write-Ahead Logging (WAL).
evidence_excerpt: Beginning with version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21), a new "Write-Ahead Log" option (hereafter referred to as "WAL") is available.

asserts: In WAL mode, readers do not block writers and vice versa, allowing concurrent reading and writing.
scope: When using the Write-Ahead Logging method.
evidence_excerpt: WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed concurrently.

asserts: The wal-index helps readers locate pages in the WAL quickly, improving performance.
scope: During use of Write-Ahead Logging method.
evidence_excerpt: A data structure called the "wal-index" is maintained in shared memory which helps readers locate pages in the WAL quickly and with a minimum of I/O. The wal-index greatly improves the performance of readers, but the use of shared memory means that all readers must exist on the same machine.
